GOVERNMENT REITERATES ITS COMMITMENT FOR REIMAGINING SKILLING
articles.full_content:
NITI Aayog released a report titled “Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047” which provides a blueprint for a skilling architecture, aligned to the needs of ‘Viksit Bharat’. The report identifies 5 key segments of learners /workforce, including NEET youth in the age group 15-29 years. This is defined as a set of young people who fall under the following categories: (i) Engaged in voluntary work/ household enterprise; (ii) Attending domestic duties; (iii) Not able to work due to health condition; (iv) Spending leisure time; and (v) Others.
In certain sections, the figure of 8.7 crore NEET youth has been misinterpreted as unemployed. The category of NEET in the report refers to those not seeking employment, and the acronym NEET stands for Not in Education, Employment or Training. Therefore, it cannot be read as a measure of joblessness or as an addition to the unemployment rate. The unemployed represent an entirely separate category, drawn from a different population base than that used for the NEET estimate.
The NITI Aayog Report has clearly stated that the database utilised in computation of these figures is based on NSS 78th Round which was collected during the COVID-19 pandemic (FY 2020–21). It was a time of disruption in the field of education and employment and hence the figures stated in the report could be a deviation from the normal trajectory. This is apparent from the fact that the youth NEET percentage is significantly lower in the most recent PLFS round (PLFS 2025).
The government is committed to robust and evidence-based policymaking. As a step to facilitate the same, Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was introduced in 2017-18, ushering in annual estimates in contrast to the earlier regime of NSSO Employment-Unemployment Surveys which were conducted once every five years and hence leaving a trail of considerable lag in actual indices. To further strengthen the evaluation and aligning with international practice, since January 2025, PLFS underwent a further improvement including the shifting of survey period to January-December calendar year cycle.
With a vision to achieve Viksit Bharat@2047, the Government is taking all measures to skill our youth and prepare them for future growth. Hence, even before the publication of the report, the Government has proactively started the implementation of the key reforms suggested in the report through the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship. Introduction of the ₹600 crore, Integrated Scheme in Skilling Architecture (ISSA) in the Union Budget 2026–27 as a precursor to the launch of the said report makes the intent of the government amply clear, which is to strengthen convergence across education, skilling, employment, and lifelong learning systems.

The report identifies 5 key segments of learners /workforce, including NEET youth in the age group 15-29 years. This is defined as a set of young people who fall under the following categories: (i) Engaged in voluntary work/ household enterprise; (ii) Attending domestic duties; (iii) Not able to work due to health condition; (iv) Spending leisure time; and (v) Others.

Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Proposes Amendments to Medical Devices Rules, 2017 to Promote Ease of Doing Business
articles.full_content:
Proposed amendments seek to simplify regulatory requirements, standardize testing fees and facilitate faster market access for eligible medical devices
The Government has undertaken key regulatory reforms in the medical device sector to promote Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) by simplifying regulatory requirements, enhancing transparency and facilitating timely access to advanced and innovative medical technologies in the country.
The reforms include amendments to the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 in three key areas—simplification of provisions relating to outsourced sterilization of medical devices, introduction of uniform testing fees and inclusion of the European Union among recognized jurisdictions for waiver of clinical investigation requirements.
Under the amended provisions of Rule 44 of the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, manufacturers availing outsourced sterilization facilities will no longer be required to obtain a separate loan licence under Rule 25, provided that the sterilization facility holds a valid licence under the Medical Devices Rules, 2017.
Earlier, manufacturers without an in-house sterilization facility were required to obtain a separate loan licence for sterilization activities. The amended provision is expected to reduce regulatory compliance requirements, documentation, approval timelines and associated costs, while enabling manufacturers to efficiently avail specialized sterilization facilities.
Further, a Ninth Schedule has been inserted in the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 prescribing uniform fees for the testing of medical devices by Medical Device Testing Laboratories. The measure will establish a standardized and transparent fee structure across laboratories, reducing ambiguity and variations in testing charges.
The standardized fee structure is expected to provide greater predictability to manufacturers and importers, minimize disputes, ensure equitable treatment of stakeholders and further strengthen transparency and efficiency in the medical device regulatory framework.
In another significant reform, Rule 63 of the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 has been amended to include the European Union (EU) among the recognized stringent regulatory jurisdictions for waiver of clinical investigation requirements for medical devices without predicate devices.
The provision presently recognizes the United States of America, United Kingdom, Australia, Canada and Japan. The inclusion of the European Union will facilitate faster access in India to eligible medical devices that have already been approved in the EU, while reducing regulatory burden and timelines for importers and manufacturers.
The reforms are expected to simplify regulatory processes, reduce compliance costs, enhance transparency and predictability, and facilitate the timely availability of advanced and innovative medical devices in the country.

The reform seeks to strike a balance between regulatory oversight and ease of doing business by simplifying the licensing framework while retaining an essential traceability mechanism for outsourced sterilization.

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will embark on official visit to Canada and USA from 25th August to 2nd September 2026
articles.full_content:
Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman and Canadian Minister of Finance and National Revenue H.E. Mr. François-Philippe Champagne to participate in inaugural Economic and Financial Dialogue between the two countries FM Smt. Sitharaman will participate in Roundtable discussions with leading investors, businesses and financial sector representatives, besides one-on-one high-level interaction with private sector during the visit to Canada and USA Union Finance Minister will lead the Indian delegation at G20 FMCBG meeting under the US G20 Presidency Union Finance Minister will also interact with Indian communities based in Toronto and Chicago to strengthen people-to-people and economic linkages
Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman will later undertake an official visit to Canada and the United States of America from 25 th August to 2 nd September 2026, with a focus on strengthening bilateral economic and financial partnerships, deepening investment linkages and advancing cooperation on shared global economic priorities.
During her visit to Toronto, Canada , Smt. Sitharaman will participate in the inaugural Economic and Financial Dialogue with H.E. Mr. François-Philippe Champagne, Minister of Finance and National Revenue of Canada. The Dialogue will provide an important platform for both sides to exchange views on macroeconomic developments, financial sector cooperation, bilateral investment opportunities and shared international priorities, and to further strengthen the economic and financial pillar of the renewed India-Canada partnership.
Bilateral discussions in recent months have also focused on opportunities in areas including energy, critical minerals, technology, innovation and resilient supply chains, alongside ongoing efforts towards a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA).
Smt. Sitharaman will participate in an Investment Roundtable with leading CEOs, Presidents and senior representatives, chief among them are from the energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals sectors. The interaction will seek to facilitate greater business-to-business linkages, identify investment opportunities and promote long-term commercial partnerships between India and Canada, including opportunities in GIFT City-IFSC.
In another Business Roundtable , the Union Finance Minister will engage with senior business leaders on opportunities for Canada-India cooperation, long-term investment and growth of the financial sector. Senior Managing Directors and Chief Executive Officers of Indian Public Sector Banks will also participate in the discussions, providing an opportunity to explore avenues for greater financial-sector collaboration and investment linkages.
